title: Allen Institute releases planet-wide satellite embeddings you can query in a browser
friendlyTitle: Ai2 releases satellite maps of the whole planet you can query in a browser
summary: The Allen Institute for AI has released OlmoEarth v1.3, an open satellite embedding model, plus precomputed annual embeddings for land and nearby coastal water at 10-meter resolution. A year of Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Landsat observations becomes one 128-number vector per pixel, or a smaller 64-number version. The institute says the 128-dimension embeddings ranked highest on 20 of 27 evaluations against AlphaEarth Foundations and Tessera v2. Weights, pretraining data, and code are open. A browser explorer lets you compare years, find similar places, or train a small classifier from a few labels and export a GeoTIFF, with no account.

The institute says the 128-number embeddings ranked highest on 20 of 27 tests against AlphaEarth Foundations and Tessera v2. The weights, the training data, and the code are open. whyItMatters: Mapping crops, fire damage, or land-use change used to mean downloading imagery and training a model. For a first look, you can now click a place and ask which other places look like it, or label a handful of points and export a map. The explorer does not replace a local check on the ground. It does remove the GPU bill from the first pass.
